content:
Looking at the first fold: the crease $AB$ makes angle $\alpha = 63°$ with the strip's edges. Folding over $AB$ reflects one part of the strip, and the two parts then meet at an angle of $180° - 2\alpha = 180° - 126° = 54°$ (the overlap forms an isosceles triangle with base angles $\alpha$).

The second fold is made along the edge of one of the layers. Reflection preserves angles, so the folded-over part again makes the same $54°$ angle with that edge line. The angle $\beta$ shown is exactly this angle between the folded flap's edge and the strip's edge.

Therefore $\beta = 180° - 2(63°) = 54°$.

\boxed{D}
